title: Idempotency lock key SHA-1 derivation vs UNIQUE-constraint SSOT — defense-in-depth only
evidence: Lock key = sha1($branchId.'|'.$idempotencyKey). Different X-Idempotency-Key values yield different SHA-1 → different cache locks. orders.idempotency_key UNIQUE constraint + QueryException catch at line 1075-1082 protects against same-key races. The 'one-bit-diff would pass lock + create two orders' framing is technically true but is by DESIGN (different keys = different intentional requests).
recommendation: Plan P1-2 over-classifies. Demote T-3 to V1.0.2 backlog or kill. Low ROI for V1.0.1 cycle.

title: Non-strict recordCashOrderMovement silently swallows errors (kiosk counter-collect path)
evidence: catch (\Throwable $e) { if ($strict) throw; Log::warning(...); } — when $strict=false (default path called from confirmCounterPayment line 260), any cash service failure (DB transient, lock contention) is logged-only and the order proceeds with NO cash_movements row. End-of-day reconcile under-counts kiosk-counter-collect cash by exactly the silently-failed orders.
recommendation: Add T-11: promote $strict=true under sim_hardware=false (default production), OR add per-failure sentinel counter + audit row tagged 'cash_movement_drop'. Without this, NF525 forensic chain misses a class of failures.
